patches.repl:
What each tool does

  • Search Everything — Search every regiment, battery, story, and battlefield location by name.
  • Ask the Historian — Ask about any regiment, place, or moment of the battle and get an answer built from this site's own historical records.
  • Documentary Mode — Follow the battle's key moments in order, with full narrative text for each -- a read-along documentary tour.
  • Compare Two Moments — Compare unit positions at two different moments of the Battle of Gettysburg side by side.
  • Camera Modes — Auto-camera and unit-follow modes: watch the battle unfold hands-free, or follow one regiment through the fighting.
  • What-If Sandbox — Drag unit positions and explore hypothetical scenarios -- for fun and imagination, not historical prediction.
  • Turning Points — The nine moments historians agree could have changed the outcome of the battle -- what happened, and what the real debate over 'what if' actually is.
  • Casualty & Strength Dashboard — Corps-by-corps strength and casualty trends across all three days of Gettysburg, built from primary-source casualty data.
  • High Ground — Compare the height of 30 battlefield landmarks, ranked by elevation. Line-of-sight maps are not shown.
  • Regimental Biography — Follow one regiment's entire three-day battle -- its commander, its casualties, and every recorded moment -- told as a single story.
  • The Ground Remembers — A heatmap of the battlefield that accumulates across all three days -- where the fighting concentrated the most, permanently.
  • Find an Ancestor — Search by state or a commander's surname to find which regiments at Gettysburg your ancestor may have served in.
  • Watch Together — Build a guided, annotated tour of the battle and share it with someone else to watch on their own.
  • Immersive Mode — Watch the battle with a procedural ambient soundscape -- cannon fire, musketry, and quiet -- generated live from the same troop density driving the map.
  • Living Ledger — Watch the human cost of the battle rise minute by minute, tied to the same casualty data behind the main map.
  • Aftermath — What happened after the battle: the retreat, the aftermath in the town, and the dedication of the Soldiers' National Cemetery.
  • For Students — An easy-to-follow walkthrough of the Battle of Gettysburg for students and classrooms.
  • Regiment Fact Sheets — Generate a printable one-page fact sheet on any regiment, for study, teaching, or reference.
  • Export a Video — Pick a stretch of the battle and export a narrated flyover video, right from your browser -- no editing software required.

Privacy · Terms · User guide (PDF)
